questions.prompt: At a STOP sign with a painted stop line, where should your first complete stop be?

options.text: At the line, before entering the crossing
Halfway through the intersection
Where your front wheels reach the crosswalk
Only where cross traffic is visible

questions.explanation: Stop at the marked line. A limited view does not remove that first stopping requirement.

questions.prompt: A STOP sign has no stop line, but a crosswalk is marked before the intersection. Where do you stop?

options.text: Beyond the crosswalk
Before entering the crosswalk
Beside the sign regardless of the crosswalk
Only after seeing another vehicle

questions.explanation: Without a stop line, stop before the near-side crosswalk. Keep the pedestrian crossing clear.

questions.prompt: At an ordinary intersection, a flashing red traffic light requires you to:

options.text: Proceed at the posted speed
Stop only for pedestrians
Stop, then follow stop-sign right-of-way rules
Wait for a green light

questions.explanation: Flashing red requires a complete stop. You may continue when the stop-sign yielding rules allow it.

questions.prompt: You approach an ordinary intersection controlled by a flashing yellow light. The road ahead is visible. Which response fits the signal?

options.text: Treat it as a green arrow
Accelerate to leave the intersection quickly
Stop until the light changes color
Proceed cautiously while checking for conflicts

questions.explanation: Flashing yellow permits cautious progress; it does not promise that the intersection is clear.

questions.prompt: A red X above a traffic lane means:

options.text: Do not drive in that lane
The lane is for faster traffic
Use the lane only to pass
The lane will open after one stop

questions.explanation: A red X closes the lane to your direction of travel.

questions.prompt: The lane-control signal over your lane changes to a steady yellow X. What should you prepare to do?

options.text: Speed up through the lane
Leave the lane safely before a red X appears
Stop in the lane immediately
Continue until another car changes lanes

questions.explanation: A steady yellow X warns you to vacate the lane safely in preparation for its closure.

questions.prompt: Your light turns green while a pedestrian who entered legally is still in the adjacent crosswalk you would turn across. What do you do?

options.text: Turn behind them without checking clearance
Sound your horn to make them hurry
Yield and let the crossing clear
Proceed because green overrides the crosswalk

questions.explanation: A green signal still requires yielding to people lawfully in the intersection or adjacent crosswalk.

questions.prompt: A steady yellow traffic signal tells you that:

options.text: Cross traffic already has unrestricted priority
You must increase speed
The signal is malfunctioning
The green movement is ending and red follows

questions.explanation: Yellow warns of the transition away from green. It is not permission to accelerate.

questions.prompt: At an uncontrolled four-way intersection, two vehicles on different roads arrive at about the same time. Who yields?

options.text: The driver with the other vehicle on their right
The driver in the larger vehicle
The driver traveling north
The driver on the right

questions.explanation: Under the ordinary equal-arrival rule, the vehicle on the left yields to the one on the right.

questions.prompt: At an uncontrolled four-way intersection, you and a vehicle to your right approach at approximately the same time. Neither is turning. What is your correct decision?

options.text: Accelerate to establish priority
Yield to the vehicle on your right
Assume the other driver will stop
Use your horn and proceed

questions.explanation: The equal-arrival rule puts the yielding duty on you because the other vehicle is to your right.

questions.prompt: Before making an unprotected left turn, you must yield to oncoming vehicles that:

options.text: Are larger than your car only
Have their headlights on only
Are close enough to create an immediate hazard
Are turning right only

questions.explanation: An unprotected left turn must wait for an adequate gap in conflicting oncoming traffic.

questions.prompt: You are waiting to turn left into a driveway. An oncoming car is close enough that turning would make its driver brake sharply. What should you do?

options.text: Turn because driveways have priority
Move halfway across and wait
Flash your lights and begin turning
Wait for a safe interval

questions.explanation: Yield to oncoming traffic posing an immediate hazard, including when turning into a driveway.

questions.prompt: When entering a highway from a private driveway, you must:

options.text: Yield to vehicles approaching on the highway
Enter before vehicles from your left
Claim priority by signaling
Yield only to trucks

questions.explanation: A driveway does not confer priority over approaching highway traffic.

questions.prompt: You want to cross a road from a private entrance. A car is approaching on the road you will cross. Which approach is correct?

options.text: Cross first because you are going straight
Yield and wait until crossing is safe
Enter slowly and make it stop
Yield only if it sounds its horn

questions.explanation: The yielding duty applies when crossing the highway as well as when joining it.

questions.prompt: At a T intersection without signs or signals, what must a driver on the road that ends do?

options.text: Turn without stopping
Yield only to traffic from the right
Stop and yield to conflicting traffic on the continuing road
Keep moving if the road looks quiet

questions.explanation: Illinois requires the driver on the terminating road to stop and yield before entering safely.

questions.prompt: Your road ends at an unsigned T intersection. A car is approaching on the continuing road from your left. Can you use the ordinary vehicle-on-the-right rule to go first?

options.text: Yes, if you are turning right
Yes, if you signal
Yes, because there is no STOP sign
No; stop and yield to the conflicting vehicle

questions.explanation: The specific T-intersection rule controls: the driver on the ending road stops and yields.

questions.prompt: Within a business or residential district, the required turn signal should run continuously for at least the final:

options.text: 100 feet before the maneuver
25 feet before the maneuver
50 feet before the maneuver
500 feet before every maneuver

questions.explanation: Illinois specifies at least 100 feet of continuous signaling within these districts.

questions.prompt: On a rural road outside a business or residential district, you plan a turn well ahead. What is the minimum continuous signaling distance?

options.text: 100 feet
200 feet
One car length
Only while you are turning

questions.explanation: Outside business and residential districts, the minimum signaling distance is 200 feet.

questions.prompt: When passing a bicyclist traveling in your direction, what minimum clearance must you maintain until safely past?

options.text: One foot
Two feet
At least three feet, and more when safety requires
The width of your mirror

questions.explanation: Three feet is a minimum, not a guarantee of safety. The clearance must continue until the pass is complete.

questions.prompt: You are passing a bicyclist. Another lane in your direction is available, a lane change is legal, and conditions make it safe and practicable. What should you do?

options.text: Stay close to the bicyclist and honk
Pass without changing lanes regardless of clearance
Let your mirror pass within one foot
Change into the available lane and maintain safe clearance

questions.explanation: The statute calls for the practicable, lawful lane change and at least three feet of safe passing clearance.

questions.prompt: Before moving from one marked lane to another, you must first:

options.text: Determine that the move can be made safely
Wait for the vehicle behind to flash its lights
Move halfway across to test the gap
Turn your signal off

questions.explanation: Lane changes require a safety check before movement. Signaling alone does not establish a safe gap.

questions.prompt: You need the next lane for an upcoming turn, but another vehicle occupies the space beside you. Which action fits the lane-change rule?

options.text: Move over because your signal gives priority
Stay in your lane until a safe move is possible
Straddle the lane marking
Force the other vehicle to slow

questions.explanation: Remain within your lane until you can change lanes safely, even if that means missing a turn.

questions.prompt: A U-turn is allowed only when it can be made:

options.text: Without using a turn signal
Before another driver notices
Safely and without interfering with other traffic
Wherever there is no painted center line

questions.explanation: Safety and noninterference are required; other signs and restrictions can still prohibit the turn.

questions.prompt: Near a hill crest, approaching drivers could see your car only from 300 feet away. Should you make a U-turn there?

options.text: Yes, if you turn quickly
Yes, if no car is currently visible
Yes, if your hazard lights are on
No; the restricted sight distance makes that location prohibited

questions.explanation: Do not U-turn near a crest or on a curve where approaching drivers cannot see the vehicle within 500 feet.

questions.prompt: Driving at the posted maximum is acceptable only if:

options.text: Your speed is also reasonable for actual conditions
Every vehicle behind you is faster
You have driven the road before
Your vehicle has good tires

questions.explanation: The posted limit does not cancel the duty to reduce speed for hazards and conditions.

questions.prompt: Heavy rain reduces visibility on a road posted at 55 mph. What should guide your speed?

options.text: Staying exactly at 55 mph
A lower speed appropriate to visibility, traffic, and road conditions
Matching the fastest driver
The speed you used yesterday

questions.explanation: Weather can require driving below the posted maximum. Choose a speed that avoids endangering others.

questions.prompt: Illinois's following-distance rule requires a gap that is:

options.text: Exactly one car length at all speeds
Whatever the vehicle behind allows
Reasonable for speed, traffic, and road conditions
Small enough to prevent any other vehicle merging

questions.explanation: The law bases a prudent gap on conditions rather than one fixed distance for every situation.

questions.prompt: Traffic speeds up while the pavement becomes slick. Your current following gap leaves little room if the car ahead brakes. What should you change?

options.text: Follow closer to see its brake lights
Keep the same gap at every speed
Use the horn instead of changing distance
Increase your space and adjust speed to conditions

questions.explanation: A gap must remain reasonable for both speed and roadway conditions. A cramped gap does not satisfy that duty.

questions.prompt: Daytime rain now requires your windshield wipers. Which lights should you use?

options.text: Headlights, with the required rear lights operating
Parking lights alone
Hazard flashers instead of headlights
No lights until sunset

questions.explanation: Weather requiring wipers triggers the headlight requirement. Parking lights do not substitute for headlights.

questions.prompt: When required headlights are on, can parking lights alone replace them?

options.text: Yes, on familiar streets
No, parking lights are not a substitute
Yes, below 30 mph
Yes, when another car is nearby

questions.explanation: Parking lamps may supplement headlights; they do not meet the requirement in their place.

questions.prompt: You pass your exit on a controlled-access highway. The shoulder behind you looks empty. What should you do?

options.text: Reverse slowly on the shoulder
Back up with hazard lights
Continue to a lawful exit and reroute
Ask a passenger to guide you while reversing

questions.explanation: Backing on the roadway or shoulder of a controlled-access highway is prohibited.

questions.prompt: A delivery van blocks your view as you prepare to reverse from a parking space. What condition must be satisfied before you back out?

options.text: Your reverse lights are on
Another driver has sounded a horn
You have waited ten seconds
You can back safely without interfering with traffic

questions.explanation: Do not reverse until you can establish that the movement is safe and will not interfere with others.

questions.prompt: At a crosswalk without operating traffic signals, a pedestrian is crossing on your half of the road. What must you do?

options.text: Stop and yield
Only slow down if they wave
Pass behind them at unchanged speed
Proceed if you are on time for the light ahead

questions.explanation: Drivers must stop and yield to a crossing pedestrian in the specified conflict area.

questions.prompt: The vehicle ahead stops at a marked crosswalk to let someone cross. The next lane looks open. May you pass it?

options.text: Yes, after sounding the horn
No; do not overtake the vehicle stopped for the pedestrian
Yes, if you drive under 15 mph
Yes, if you cannot see the pedestrian

questions.explanation: Passing a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian at such a crosswalk is prohibited; the vehicle may hide the person crossing.

questions.prompt: On a two-lane, two-way road, a school bus stops to unload with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. Drivers approaching from either direction must:

options.text: Proceed if they see no children
Stop only when behind the bus
Stop before reaching the bus
Slow down but keep moving

questions.explanation: The stop requirement applies from both directions on this road while the bus uses its required stopping signals.

questions.prompt: A school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing on the opposite side of a four-lane road with two lanes in each direction. What does Illinois's opposing-roadway exception mean?

options.text: You may pass a bus stopped directly ahead of you
All drivers in both directions may ignore the bus
Only vehicles in the nearest lane must stop
Opposing traffic need not stop for that bus, but must still drive safely

questions.explanation: The exception covers meeting the bus in the opposing roadway on this four-or-more-lane configuration; it does not cover following it.

questions.prompt: An ambulance with its emergency lights and siren approaches from behind. Which response is appropriate?

options.text: Yield, move toward the right edge clear of intersections, and stop if needed for safe passage
Stop in the middle of the intersection
Race to the next light
Move left into oncoming traffic

questions.explanation: Make room at the right edge, clear of intersections, and stop when necessary for the ambulance to pass safely.

questions.prompt: You approach a stopped police car with emergency lights on a four-lane highway. The lane farther from it is clear and a safe lane change is possible. What should you do?

options.text: Keep speed and stay beside it
Move to the farther lane, reduce speed, and pass cautiously with space
Stop next to the police car
Only change lanes if an officer waves

questions.explanation: Move over when safe and possible, reduce speed, and leave a safe distance past the emergency scene.

questions.prompt: At 8 a.m. on a school day, children are nearby enough to create a hazard in a properly signed school zone. The special maximum is:

options.text: 30 mph
25 mph
20 mph
35 mph

questions.explanation: Under these school-zone conditions, the special limit is 20 mph. Conditions may require an even slower safe speed.

questions.prompt: At 9 a.m. on a school day, you enter a signed school zone with children close to the road. A vehicle behind pressures you to speed up. What should you do?

options.text: Match the following driver's speed
Go 25 mph if no crossing guard appears
Speed up until a child enters the road
Respect the 20 mph maximum and slow further if needed

questions.explanation: Pressure from another driver does not remove the school-zone limit or your duty to respond safely to children.

questions.prompt: You leave an urban driveway across a sidewalk. No pedestrian is visible. What is required before crossing the sidewalk?

options.text: Stop before entering the sidewalk area and check for people
Keep moving if you are under 5 mph
Stop only if someone waves
Sound the horn and continue

questions.explanation: The urban-driveway rule requires the stop before the sidewalk, not only when a pedestrian is visible.

questions.prompt: An urban alley has no sidewalk at its exit. Where should you make the required stop before entering the street?

options.text: Anywhere halfway down the alley
At the point nearest the street where approaching traffic is visible
After your front wheels enter a travel lane
Only when another vehicle is coming

questions.explanation: Without a sidewalk area, stop nearest the street where you can see approaching traffic; then yield before entering.

questions.prompt: For ordinary parking, how far must your vehicle be from a fire hydrant?

options.text: At least 5 feet
At least 10 feet
At least 15 feet
At least 8 feet

questions.explanation: Parking within 15 feet of a hydrant is prohibited, subject to statutory exceptions and controlling directions.

questions.prompt: You want to park beside a vehicle already parked at the curb while you visit a shop. Is that permitted just because you leave your hazard lights on?

options.text: Yes, for five minutes
Yes, if someone stays in the car
Yes, on a quiet street
No; hazard lights do not authorize double parking

questions.explanation: Ordinary double parking on the roadway side of a curbside vehicle is prohibited.

questions.prompt: For ordinary parallel parking on a two-way road with a curb, the right wheels should be:

options.text: Parallel to and within 12 inches of the right curb
Against the left curb facing traffic
At least 24 inches from the curb
Angled into the traffic lane

questions.explanation: The general rule places the right wheels parallel to the right curb and within 12 inches.

questions.prompt: Parallel parking is allowed on both sides of a one-way street, with no different local rule. Which direction should your parked car face?

options.text: Either direction
The authorized direction of traffic
Against traffic on the left side
Toward the nearest intersection

questions.explanation: The one-way rule allows either curb where permitted, but the vehicle must face the authorized traffic direction.

questions.prompt: Before leaving a normally keyed car unattended, which action is part of the legal requirement?

options.text: Leave the key for emergency access
Keep the engine idling
Set the brake and shut off and secure the ignition
Leave the car in neutral

questions.explanation: Ordinarily, stop the engine, secure the ignition, remove its key, and set the brake before leaving.

questions.prompt: You park facing downhill on a noticeable slope beside a curb and will leave the car. Beyond securing the engine and setting the brake, how should you position the front wheels?

options.text: Leave the front wheels straight in every situation
Aim the front wheels toward moving traffic
Leave the transmission in neutral
Toward the curb

questions.explanation: On a grade, Illinois requires positioning the wheels toward the curb or roadside. In this downhill example, turn them toward the curb.

questions.prompt: You are parked beside a bicycle lane. A cyclist is approaching as you reach for the traffic-side door. What should you do?

options.text: Keep the door closed until opening it is safe and will not interfere
Open quickly so the cyclist can react
Crack the door to make the cyclist stop
Open because parked vehicles have priority

questions.explanation: Check for traffic, including bicycles. A traffic-side door may open only when safe and without interfering with moving traffic.

questions.prompt: You borrow a family member's car displaying their disability placard. The authorized holder is not with you. May you use a reserved accessible space for your own shopping?

options.text: Yes, because the placard is visible
No; the placard does not transfer the holder's parking privileges to you
Yes, for a brief errand
Yes, if other accessible spaces remain

questions.explanation: The credential is not transferable. Using the privilege requires the authorized holder's qualifying presence and entry or exit.
